decks.domain: Special driving conditions and your vehicle

cards.front: In what weather do most crashes happen?
cards.back: Most crashes happen in clear weather rather than in snow, rain or fog, so a pleasant day can be just as deadly.

cards.front: What do many drivers do when a collision seems about to happen?
cards.back: When a collision seems about to happen, many drivers panic and do nothing, yet there is almost always some action that can avoid the crash or lessen it.

cards.front: What are the three ways to avoid a collision?
cards.back: To avoid a collision a driver has three options: stop, turn, or speed up.

cards.front: Why read your owner's manual about brakes?
cards.back: Read your vehicle owner's manual to learn how its antilock braking system works, since antilock brakes let you stop without skidding.

cards.front: How do you stop quickly with antilock brakes?
cards.back: To stop quickly with antilock brakes, press the brake pedal as hard as you can and keep firm pressure on it, without letting up even when the pedal pushes back.

cards.front: How do you stop quickly without antilock brakes?
cards.back: To stop quickly without antilock brakes, brake as hard as you can without locking the wheels, since braking too hard or too long can cause a skid.

cards.front: Without antilock brakes, what do you do if the wheels lock?
cards.back: Without antilock brakes, if the wheels lock and you feel a skid, let up on the pedal quickly, then press down again once the skid stops, repeating until the car stops.

cards.front: How do antilock brakes change an emergency stop?
cards.back: In an emergency with antilock brakes the wheels do not lock and the car can still be steered, while without them all wheels may lock and the skidding car cannot be steered properly.

cards.front: Should you pump antilock brakes when the pedal pulses?
cards.back: Never pump the brake pedal in a car with antilock brakes, even when the pedal pulses; the pulsing is the system pumping the brakes faster than you could.

cards.front: What should your foot do when antilock brakes pulse and rattle?
cards.back: With antilock brakes, keep your foot firmly on the pedal despite the pulsing and noise, because easing off ruins the system's advantage.

cards.front: Should antilock brakes make you drive more aggressively?
cards.back: Never drive a car with antilock brakes more aggressively than one without them.

decks.domain: Special driving conditions and your vehicle

cards.front: If you cannot stop in time, what should you do?
cards.back: In most cases you can turn your vehicle faster than you can stop it, so if you cannot stop in time, steer around the hazard and brake only if you must.

cards.front: Where should your hands be for quick turns?
cards.back: For quick turns, grip the wheel with both hands on opposite sides at about the nine o'clock and three o'clock positions, which also keeps your wrists and forearms out of the air bag's main impact area.

cards.front: How do your hands move in a quick left turn?
cards.back: For a quick evasive turn to the left, the right hand swings from three o'clock toward nine o'clock as far as needed while the left hand slides toward the bottom of the wheel to steady the grip.

cards.front: How do you regain your lane after clearing a hazard?
cards.back: As you clear the hazard, turn the wheel back to the right to regain your lane, then left just enough to straighten out, returning your hands to nine and three; for a quick right turn, mirror every step.

cards.front: What must you be ready for after steering away from a hazard?
cards.back: After steering away from a hazard, be ready to keep control and steer where you want the car to go, because some drivers dodge one crash only to cause another.

cards.front: Can you steer while braking with antilock brakes?
cards.back: With antilock brakes you can steer while braking without skidding, which helps when you must swerve and stop or slow quickly.

cards.front: Without antilock brakes, how do you turn quickly?
cards.back: Without antilock brakes, to turn quickly you must let up on the brake pedal and then turn the wheel.

cards.front: Why brake before a quick turn without antilock brakes?
cards.back: Braking before a quick turn without antilock brakes slows the car and shifts weight onto the front tires, which lets it turn faster.

cards.front: What should you do if the front wheels lock?
cards.back: Stop braking if you feel the front wheels lock, and do not turn so sharply that the car can only plow straight ahead.

cards.front: Is it better to drive off the road or crash head-on?
cards.back: It is generally better to drive off the road than to crash head-on into another vehicle.

cards.front: When can speeding up be the right move?
cards.back: Speeding up can be the right move when another vehicle is about to hit you from the side or behind and there is room ahead, but slow down once the danger passes.

cards.front: Why should you not jerk the wheel in an emergency?
cards.back: Do not freeze at the wheel or jerk it suddenly in an emergency, because a jerk can send you into another object or off the road and into a rollover.

cards.front: How should you use antilock braking to avoid an obstacle?
cards.back: Use the antilock system's nonskid ability to steer around the obstacle that made you brake, and keep steering to a safe place once past it.

cards.front: How can you practice antilock braking?
cards.back: To practice antilock braking, use a big empty lot without curbs or many light poles, drive about twenty miles per hour, slam the brakes and steer, later steering around a cardboard box as a target.

decks.domain: Special driving conditions and your vehicle

cards.front: What season is peak for deer crashes?
cards.back: Fall is the peak season for deer crashes, because autumn's mating and hunting seasons make deer more active and likely to wander.

cards.front: Which animal crashes are the most dangerous and costly?
cards.back: Crashes with deer are generally the most dangerous and costly kind of animal crash.

cards.front: When and where should you watch most for deer?
cards.back: Be especially alert for deer at dusk and dawn, when they come out to feed, and near woods and water.

cards.front: You see one deer. What should you expect?
cards.back: If you see one deer, expect that several others may be close by.

cards.front: When can animal crashes happen?
cards.back: Animal crashes can happen in any season and with any animal, from opossums and rabbits to dogs, and while many deer crashes occur at night, they can happen at any hour.

cards.front: Is there a foolproof way to keep deer off highways?
cards.back: No foolproof method has been found to keep deer and other wild animals off highways.

cards.front: How can you avoid deer?
cards.back: To avoid deer, heed deer crossing signs, look far down the road and well off to each side, and at night use high beams when you can to light the road edges.

cards.front: What should you scan the roadsides for at night?
cards.back: Scan the roadsides for your headlights reflecting in a deer's eyes.

cards.front: What should you do if you have time to avoid an animal?
cards.back: If you have time to avoid an animal ahead, slow down, tap your brakes to warn drivers behind you, and sound your horn.

cards.front: Why not flash your lights at a deer?
cards.back: Deer tend to fixate on headlights, so flashing your lights at one may make it freeze in the road.

cards.front: How hard should you brake for an animal with no one close behind?
cards.back: If no vehicle is close behind you, brake hard for an animal but do not lock the wheels into a skid.

cards.front: Should you swerve if hitting an animal seems unavoidable?
cards.back: If hitting an animal seems unavoidable, do not swerve, since swerving may raise your risk of injury; keep the car under control and on the road.

cards.front: Whom do you tell after hitting a deer or farm animal?
cards.back: Report a crash with a large animal such as a deer or farm animal to the police.

cards.front: What should you do after hitting a pet near homes?
cards.back: If you hit a domestic pet near homes, try to let the owner know if you can.

decks.module: The driver and fitness to drive
decks.domain: Special driving conditions and your vehicle

cards.front: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
cards.back: Human error is the single most common cause of traffic crashes, and the leading factors are excessive speed, lack of concentration and improper evasive action.

cards.front: What are the three parts of the highway system?
cards.back: Safe driving depends on three parts of the highway system, the driver, the vehicle and the road, and neglecting any of them contributes to most crashes.

cards.front: How does a good driver differ from a careless one?
cards.back: A good driver takes pride in caring for the vehicle, obeys traffic laws and respects others, while a careless driver neglects all three.

cards.front: How many yearly crashes does the manual tie to poor habits?
cards.back: The manual attributes about one hundred sixty thousand crashes reported to the Department of Safety each year to poor driving habits.

cards.front: What does being in shape to drive mean?
cards.back: Being in shape to drive means seeing clearly, being rested, being free of drugs, and being healthy and emotionally fit.

cards.front: Which temporary conditions can make you unsafe?
cards.back: Temporary conditions such as anger, worry, frustration, fatigue or even a cold can make you an unsafe driver.

cards.front: What should you do if you feel unwell?
cards.back: If you feel unwell, even from a stiff neck, cough or sore leg, let someone else drive.

cards.front: When may a person with epilepsy drive in Tennessee?
cards.back: In Tennessee, a person with epilepsy may drive if under a doctor's care and seizure-free for at least six months.

cards.front: When should a diabetic on insulin stay off the road?
cards.back: A diabetic on insulin should stay off the road whenever an insulin reaction, blackout, convulsion or shock is possible, for example after skipping a meal.

cards.front: Who with heart problems should not drive?
cards.back: People with heart disease, high blood pressure or circulation problems who risk blackouts, fainting or a heart attack should not drive, and anyone treated for a heart condition should ask a doctor about driving.

cards.front: What should you do if you are angry or impatient before driving?
cards.back: If you are angry or excited, give yourself time to calm down before driving, and if you are impatient, plan extra time for trips so delays do not tempt you to speed.

cards.front: Can a skilled driver drive safely when buzzed?
cards.back: No one, regardless of skill or experience, can drive safely when buzzed or impaired by alcohol or drugs.

decks.domain: Special driving conditions and your vehicle confusables and continuation details

cards.front: How does night affect everyone's vision?
cards.back: Everyone sees worse at night, and some drivers struggle with the glare of oncoming headlights.

cards.front: What should you do if you struggle to see at night?
cards.back: If you have trouble seeing at night, limit night driving to what is necessary and be very careful when you do.

cards.front: When does judging distance and speed matter most?
cards.back: Judging distance and speed takes practice and matters most when merging and when judging gaps to pass on two-lane roads.

cards.front: How often should an eye specialist check your eyes?
cards.back: Because seeing well is so important, have your eyes checked by an eye specialist every year or two.

cards.front: What does the corrective lens restriction require?
cards.back: If your license shows the corrective lens restriction, code one, you must wear your glasses or contacts at all times while driving, or you could be ticketed and fined.

cards.front: Should you wear your glasses even on short trips?
cards.back: If you need glasses or contacts, wear them even on short trips, and keep a spare pair in the vehicle.

cards.front: Should you wear dark sunglasses at night?
cards.back: Do not wear dark sunglasses or tinted contact lenses at night, since they cut the light you need to see.

cards.front: How does hearing help a driver?
cards.back: Hearing helps you notice horns, sirens and screeching tires, and hearing-impaired drivers can compensate with their vision.

cards.front: How can you avoid fatigue before a long trip?
cards.back: To avoid fatigue, get a normal night's sleep, eat lightly before a long trip, avoid medicine that causes drowsiness, and try not to drive when you would normally be asleep.

cards.front: How often should you stop on long drives?
cards.back: On long drives, stop for a break every hour or more often if needed, walking around and getting fresh air and a drink.

cards.front: What should you do if you feel sleepy while driving?
cards.back: Never drive while sleepy; pulling over for a few hours of sleep beats gambling that you can stay awake.

decks.domain: Special driving conditions and your vehicle confusables and continuation details

cards.front: Which signs mean a mechanic should check your brakes?
cards.back: Have a mechanic check your brakes if they seem weak, are noisy, smell odd or the pedal sinks to the floor.

cards.front: How should you check your lights?
cards.back: Check turn signals, brake lights, taillights and headlights from outside the vehicle.

cards.front: When do batteries run down faster?
cards.back: Batteries run down faster in cold or damp weather, and keeping jumper cables in the car can get you started again.

cards.front: Why fix a cracked windshield?
cards.back: Repair or replace a damaged windshield, since cracked glass can break in a minor collision, and replace wiper blades that no longer clear the glass.

cards.front: When should you check washer fluid?
cards.back: Check the non-freezing washer fluid level each time you fill up with gas, and clean the windshield at gas stops so sun or headlights do not blur your view.

cards.front: What can worn or bald tires do?
cards.back: Worn or bald tires lengthen stopping distance, make turning harder on wet roads, raise the chance of a flat and can cause hydroplaning.

cards.front: How does the penny test work?
cards.back: In the penny test, insert a penny head first into the tread; if the tread does not reach Lincoln's head, two thirty-seconds inch, the tire is illegal and unsafe and must be replaced.

cards.front: What do unbalanced tires and low pressure cause?
cards.back: Unbalanced tires and low pressure wear tires faster, waste fuel and make the vehicle harder to steer and stop.

cards.front: Which tire pressure should you use?
cards.back: Use the recommended tire pressure on the sticker in the driver's door jamb, not the pressure printed on the tire, which is only the tire's maximum.

cards.front: What pressure should you use for aftermarket tires of a different size?
cards.back: If you have put on aftermarket tires of a different size, ask the tire maker or installer for the right pressure, since the door-jamb figure no longer applies.

cards.front: What signs mean the shocks need checking?
cards.back: If the car keeps bouncing after a bump or a stop, or is hard to control, have a mechanic check the shocks and suspension.

decks.domain: Special driving conditions and your vehicle

cards.front: Why never turn the ignition to lock while moving?
cards.back: Never turn the ignition to the lock position while the car is moving, because the steering wheel will lock and you will lose control.

cards.front: What can a sleepy feeling while driving signal?
cards.back: A sleepy feeling while driving or riding may mean an exhaust leak, which must be fixed at once because exhaust gases can kill inside a vehicle in a very short time.

cards.front: Where must you never run the engine?
cards.back: Never run the engine in a closed garage or wherever the tailpipe may be blocked, including when the car is stuck in mud or snow.

cards.front: What should you do when idling for a long time?
cards.back: When idling for a long time, open a window for fresh air, and never sleep or sit with the engine running during an extended rest stop.

cards.front: When should you check the radiator?
cards.back: Check the radiator only when the engine is cool, and keep coolant at the level the owner's manual recommends to prevent overheating or freezing.

cards.front: How much gas should you have before a long trip?
cards.back: Make sure your vehicle has at least a half tank of gas before any trip of significant length.

cards.front: Why keep loose objects off the floor?
cards.back: Keep loose objects off the floor where they could roll under the brake pedal, and secure items that could hit someone in a sudden stop.

cards.front: What is the horn for?
cards.back: Use the horn only as a warning to others.

decks.domain: Special driving conditions and your vehicle confusables and continuation details

cards.front: How big a cushion should you keep behind the car ahead?
cards.back: Keep at least a two-second cushion behind the vehicle ahead, and more when conditions are hazardous.

cards.front: Why do multi-vehicle crashes happen in traffic flow?
cards.back: Vehicles moving the same direction at the same speed cannot hit one another, and multi-vehicle crashes often happen when drivers go faster or slower than traffic.

cards.front: Where should you slow down for crowds and traffic?
cards.back: Slow down where people and traffic gather, such as when brake lights come on several cars ahead, in shopping centers and downtown areas, and at rush hour.

cards.front: Why adjust speed on narrow bridges and in tunnels?
cards.back: On narrow bridges and in tunnels, approaching vehicles pass closer together, so adjust your speed.

cards.front: What should you watch for near schools and playgrounds?
cards.back: Near schools, playgrounds and residential streets, always watch for children who may cross, run or ride into the street without looking.

cards.front: What must you check at railroad crossings?
cards.back: At railroad crossings, make sure no train is coming and you have room to get across, and slow down on bumpy crossings.

cards.front: What should good drivers do after moving to a new state?
cards.back: Good drivers review the manual periodically for law changes and study the driver manual of any new state they move to, even when no test is required.

recap_hooks.text: To avoid a collision you can stop, turn or speed up, and with antilock brakes you press hard and never pump.
You can usually turn faster than you can stop, so steer around a hazard with your hands at nine and three.
Fall is peak deer season, and if hitting an animal seems unavoidable, do not swerve.

recaps.module: The driver and fitness to drive

recap_hooks.text: Human error causes most crashes, led by speed, poor concentration and wrong evasive moves.
With a corrective lens restriction you must wear your lenses at all times while driving.
If the penny test shows Lincoln's whole head, the tire must be replaced.
Never run the engine where the tailpipe may be blocked, and never lock the ignition while moving.
Moving at the same speed as traffic prevents multi-vehicle crashes.
